questions.stem: A political party is best defined as an organised group which

options.text: seeks to influence government policy without contesting elections
seeks to capture and exercise governmental power by contesting elections
is formed solely to defend the cultural heritage of one ethnic group
is appointed by the President to advise on national honours

questions.explanation: The defining purpose of a party is to form government. It recruits candidates, publishes a manifesto and asks the electorate for power. That is why section 221 of the 1999 Constitution reserves canvassing for votes to registered political parties.

distractorRationale.a: Influencing policy without seeking office is the definition of a pressure group, not a party
distractorRationale.c: A cultural association is not a party, and the Constitution forbids parties confined to one ethnic group
distractorRationale.d: An advisory body appointed by the President is not a political party

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of a political party?

options.text: Adjudicating disputes between citizens in a court of law
Printing the national currency
Aggregating the interests of different groups into a manifesto
Commanding the armed forces in wartime

questions.explanation: Interest aggregation is a core party function: a party collects scattered demands — from farmers, traders, workers, regions — and turns them into a single programme voters can accept or reject. Courts, the Central Bank and the Commander-in-Chief perform the other tasks listed.

distractorRationale.a: Adjudication is a function of the judiciary, not of parties
distractorRationale.b: Issuing currency is a function of the Central Bank of Nigeria
distractorRationale.d: Command of the armed forces belongs to the President as Commander-in-Chief

questions.stem: The aborted Third Republic in Nigeria operated a

options.text: one-party system by constitutional provision
two-party system imposed by the military government
multi-party system with five registered parties
no-party system in which only independent candidates could stand

questions.explanation: General Ibrahim Babangida's transition programme registered only two parties, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and the National Republican Convention (NRC). That was a legally imposed two-party system, not one that grew from voter choice. The June 1993 presidential election was later annulled and the republic aborted.

distractorRationale.a: Nigeria has never run a one-party republic
distractorRationale.c: Five registered parties describes the Second Republic, not the Third
distractorRationale.d: Independent candidacy was not the arrangement; two parties were created by the regime

questions.stem: The three major political parties of Nigeria's First Republic were the

options.text: NPN, UPN and NPP
NPC, NCNC and AG
PDP, APC and APGA
SDP, NRC and PRP

questions.explanation: The Northern People's Congress (NPC), the National Council of Nigerian Citizens (NCNC) and the Action Group (AG) were the three dominant parties of the First Republic, based respectively in the North, East and West. Learn the initials in full; examiners treat a wrong expansion as a wrong answer.

distractorRationale.a: NPN, UPN and NPP were the leading parties of the Second Republic (1979–1983)
distractorRationale.c: PDP and APC belong to the Fourth Republic; APGA is a later regional party
distractorRationale.d: SDP and NRC were the two parties of the aborted Third Republic; PRP was a Second Republic party

questions.stem: The All Progressives Congress (APC) was formed in 2013 by a merger that included the

options.text: Action Group, NCNC and Northern People's Congress
Action Congress of Nigeria, Congress for Progressive Change and All Nigeria Peoples Party
Unity Party of Nigeria and Nigerian People's Party only
Social Democratic Party and National Republican Convention

questions.explanation: The APC was created in February 2013 from a merger of the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN), the Congress for Progressive Change (CPC), the All Nigeria Peoples Party (ANPP) and a faction of APGA. It went on to win the 2015 presidential election, the first time an opposition party had defeated an incumbent Nigerian president at the ballot box.

distractorRationale.a: AG, NCNC and NPC belong to the First Republic, half a century earlier
distractorRationale.c: UPN and NPP were Second Republic parties and were not parties to the 2013 merger
distractorRationale.d: SDP and NRC were the imposed two parties of the aborted Third Republic

questions.stem: Nigeria's Fourth Republic is correctly described as a two-party system because the APC and the PDP dominate national elections.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. A two-party system exists where the law or the structure of competition confines power to two parties, as with SDP and NRC in 1993. The Fourth Republic permits many registered parties; APC and PDP dominate in practice, but other parties contest and sometimes win seats. Dominance is not the same as a two-party system.

distractorRationale.a: Students often equate the two biggest parties with a two-party system; the legal arrangement remains multi-party
